# bhop-godot

A bunnyhop movement controller for **Godot 4.x / GDScript**, reproducing CS:GO's
tick-based movement physics with enough fidelity that a player can strafe and
bunnyhop at the same speeds and within the same timing windows as the real game.

Not a game. There is no level, HUD art, networking, or weapon system — just a
movement simulation, a driver, and a flat test floor.

---

## Provenance: this was vibe coded

**Written with AI assistance, not by hand.** The implementation was generated by
an LLM assistant working from a written specification and a study of the CS:GO
movement source. A human directed the requirements, made the design calls, and
decided which engine behaviours to reproduce versus deliberately diverge from.

What that means for you as a reader:

- The code has **not** been reviewed by a second human. Treat it as
  unreviewed-generated code, not as battle-tested.
- The physics **is** verified — by 40,888 automated assertions across three
  headless suites, including a closed-form check of the acceleration law against
  a literal port of the original C++. Those tests are the reason to trust the
  behaviour; the prose is not.
- The design rationale, the source citations, and every known divergence are in
  [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md). That document is the real specification — this README is
  the summary.
- If you are extending this, read `PLAN.md` first. The code is a consequence of
  it, and several non-obvious choices only make sense against the reasoning
  recorded there.

---

## Status

All three suites pass from a clean checkout with no build artifacts:

```
test_air_gain    40804 checks, 0 failures
test_bhop           49 checks, 0 failures
test_live           35 checks, 0 failures
```

The load-bearing measurement: across 900 ticks and 10 bunnyhops, horizontal
speed never dropped by a single float epsilon (**worst per-tick drop
0.000000 m/s**). That is the perfect bhop working exactly as specified.

## Quick start

```bash
# run the game
godot --path .

# run the checks
godot --headless --path . --script res://test/test_air_gain.gd
godot --headless --path . --script res://test/test_bhop.gd
godot --headless --path . --script res://test/test_live.gd
```

Verified against **Godot 4.7.2-stable**. The project also runs clean from a bare
checkout with no import pass — scripts reference each other via `preload` rather
than the gitignored `class_name` registry, so a fresh clone does not fail to
parse.

### Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `W` `A` `S` `D` | move |
| mouse | look |
| `SPACE` | jump (hold to autohop) |
| `B` | toggle autohop (`sv_autobunnyhopping`) |
| `R` | toggle bunnyhop speed cap (`sv_enablebunnyhopping`) |
| `C` | toggle CS:GO hard ground clamp |
| `G` | cycle `max_speed` 320 ↔ 260 u/s |
| `ENTER` | respawn |
| `ESC` | release mouse |

The floor is a generated checker texture. That is deliberate: on a flat
single-colour plane 8 m/s and 18 m/s look identical, and you cannot tell whether
speed gain is working. The marker posts give absolute distance.

---

## How it fits together

```
project.godot    128 tick (physics_ticks_per_second), jitter fix 0
main.tscn        root scene: sky, sun, checker floor, markers, player, HUD
src/
  cs_movement.gd   pure simulation. RefCounted, no Node/Input dependency.
  bhop_player.gd   Node3D driver. Samples input once per tick, runs the sim,
                   provides collision via a box sweep through the physics server.
  test_floor.gd    generated checker texture
  hud.gd           live telemetry
test/             three headless suites
```

Two things are worth knowing before reading the code:

**The simulation is pure.** `cs_movement.gd` has no `Node` and no `Input`. It
receives `(dt, buttons, view_angles)` and returns state. Collision is delegated
to an injected object exposing a single `_sweep()`. That is what lets the same
behaviour be tested against a stub ground plane *and* real Godot physics, and
having both agree is the only evidence the collision abstraction is sound.

**It is not a `CharacterBody3D`.** `move_and_slide` owns floor state, snapping
and velocity rewriting, all of which destroy the perfect-bhop invariant (a jump
that fires before ground movement must leave horizontal velocity untouched).
Movement is therefore integrated and swept by hand.

### The bunnyhop in one line

The jump handler clears the ground state *before* the ground-movement branch is
evaluated, so friction and the ground speed clamp never run that tick. Air
movement is additive only, so horizontal velocity survives intact.

Ground detection is deliberately one tick late — evaluated at the end of tick N,
consumed at the start of tick N+1. That one-tick delay **is** the CS:GO
performance window. Removing it silently turns the model into CS2's.

---

## Tuning

Everything in Source units (`1 u = 1 inch = 0.0254 m`) is defined once in
`src/cs_movement.gd` and converted at the constant table. Per-second constants
(friction, acceleration, timers) carry over **numerically unchanged** — only
distances convert. An agent that "converts" `sv_accelerate` has introduced a bug.

The most useful knobs, exposed on the player node:

| Property | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `autobunnyhopping` | on | hold jump to bhop |
| `enable_bunnyhopping` | on | off applies the 1.1× clamp on every jump |
| `max_speed_units` | 320 | 320 is the CS:GO source value, 260 is CS2 |
| `csgo_ground_clamp` | off | on restores CS:GO's hard total-speed ground clamp |
| `stamina_enabled` | off | CS:GO's landing penalty; shipped default 80 is very punishing |
| `speed_cap` | 0 | 0 = uncapped, which is what a bhop server actually gives you |

---

## Known limitations

Read these before assuming a difference is a bug.

- **`max_speed` is unresolved.** The movement source ships `sv_maxspeed = 320`;
  CS2 uses 260; the brief quoted 260 with a ~285 u/s strafe top speed. The
  current default is the source value. It is the one number most worth pinning
  to a measured target. See `PLAN.md` §6.7.2.
- **Ground strafing diverges from CS:GO on purpose.** CS:GO hard-clamps *total*
  ground speed, so it genuinely cannot exceed `max_speed`; this project uses the
  per-direction cap so it can, as specified. That also softens missed-hop
  punishment. `C` restores the source behaviour exactly. See `PLAN.md` §6.7.
- **Gravity, stamina, and the `1.1×` clamp were implemented from the movement
  source and cross-checked against two independent documents**, but the visual
  result has not been compared side by side with the real game.
- **Not implemented:** stairs and step-up corner cases, slope walking, crouch and
  jumpbugs, water, ladders, networking. The floor is flat by design.
- **`m_flVelocityModifier`'s reduction site is unknown** — it lives outside the
  movement layer. Only the recovery half is implemented, so the exported
  `landing_penalty` defaults to 0.
- **Rendering was never verified visually.** The environment, sky, floor and HUD
  are asserted structurally by `test_live.gd`, but no screenshot has been
  captured. If the floor looks flat, the checker texture failed to generate.
